chapters.title: Who Is My Neighbor?
chapters.html:
Luke 10

The Seventy-Two

1After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them on ahead of Him, two by two, into every town and place where He Himself was about to go.

2He said to them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few; so ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into His harvest.

3Go on your way. I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.

4Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals, and greet no one on the road.

5Whatever house you enter, first say, 'Peace to this house.'

6If someone who loves peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.

7Stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they give you, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.

8Whenever you enter a town and they welcome you, eat what is set before you,

9heal the sick in it, and say to them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'

10But whenever you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,

11'Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near.'

12I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.

13"Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

14But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.

15You, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? You will be brought down to Hades.

16"Whoever listens to you listens to Me, and whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me."

17The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name!"

18He said to them, "I watched Satan fall like lightning from heaven.

19I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy; and nothing will harm you.

20Yet do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven."

Revealed to Little Children

21In that same hour He rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and the understanding and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was Your good pleasure.

22All things have been handed over to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him."

23Turning to the disciples, He said privately, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.

24For I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it."

The Good Samaritan

25A lawyer stood up to test Him, saying, "Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"

26He said to him, "What is written in the law? How do you read it?"

27He answered, "'You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind,' and 'your neighbor as yourself.'"

28He said to him, "You have answered rightly; do this, and you will live."

29But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, "Then who is my neighbor?"

30Jesus replied, "A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who stripped him, beat him and went away, leaving him half dead.

31By chance a priest was going down that road, and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

32So too a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.

33But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was, and when he saw him, he had compassion.

34He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn and took care of him.

35The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, and said, 'Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.'

36Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?"

37He said, "The one who showed him mercy." Jesus said to him, "Go and do the same."

Martha and Mary

38As they went on their way, He entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed Him.

39She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to His word.

40But Martha was distracted with much serving. She came up and said, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her, then, to help me."

41The Lord answered her, "Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things;

42but few things are needed, or only one. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her."

Notes

  • vv1–12 "seventy-two… lambs among wolves… the worker deserves his wages… more bearable on that day for Sodom" — hebdomēkonta dyo, seventy-two; the edition reads two here and in v17 and marks it as a place where manuscripts differ. Seventy were the elders chosen to share Moses' work, Gather for Me seventy men of the elders of Israel (Numbers 11:16). Arnas, lambs, where Matthew has sheep (Matthew 10:16). Huios eirēnēs, someone who loves peace, word for word a son of peace. Sodom was destroyed with sulfur and fire, from the LORD, from the heavens (Genesis 19:24).

  • vv13–16 "Woe to you, Chorazin… down to Hades… whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me" — as Matthew 11:21–23. Capernaum's pride is the king of Babylon's, How you have fallen from heaven… But you are brought down to Sheol (Isaiah 14:12, 15).

  • vv17–20 "I watched Satan fall like lightning from heaven… to tread on snakes and scorpions… your names are written in heaven" — the fall is Isaiah's word again, How you have fallen from heaven, Day Star (Isaiah 14:12). To tread, as the psalm says, you will trample the young lion and the serpent (Psalm 91:13). The book of names, as Moses asked to be blotted out from Your book that You have written (Exodus 32:32).

  • vv21–24 "He rejoiced in the Holy Spirit… revealed them to little children… many prophets and kings" — ēgalliasato, He rejoiced, the word of Mary's my spirit rejoices (1:47). The prayer is Matthew 11:25–27; kings where Matthew has righteous people (Matthew 13:17).

  • vv25–29 "what must I do to inherit eternal life?… do this, and you will live… who is my neighbor?" — the lawyer answers with Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18, joined; in Mark it is Jesus who joins them (Mark 12:29–31). Do this, and you will live is the law's own word, the person who does them shall live by them (Leviticus 18:5).

  • vv30–37 "going down from Jerusalem to Jericho… a Samaritan… pouring on oil and wine… The one who showed him mercy" — the priest and the Levite serve the temple; the Samaritan is from the people Jews and Samaritans held apart (9:52–53). In Chronicles the men of Samaria clothed, fed and anointed captives of Judah and brought them home (2 Chronicles 28:15). The lawyer asked who is my neighbor?; Jesus asks who proved to be one. The lawyer will not say the Samaritan.

  • vv38–42 "Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet… Martha was distracted with much serving… few things are needed, or only one" — at the Lord's feet, the place of a disciple (8:35). Periespato, was distracted, word for word was pulled about. Oligōn de estin chreia ē henos, few things are needed, or only one: the edition prints both and marks the words as a place where manuscripts differ. Tēn agathēn merida, the good portion, a share of a meal, or a share of an inheritance.

chapters.title: Lord, Teach Us to Pray
chapters.html:
Luke 11

The Prayer

1Once He was praying in a certain place, and when He had finished, one of His disciples said to Him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."

2He said to them, "When you pray, say:

Father,
hallowed be Your name.
Your kingdom come.

3Give us each day our daily bread,

4and forgive us our sins,
for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us;
and lead us not into temptation."

5He said to them, "Which of you who has a friend will go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves,

6for a friend of mine has arrived from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';

7and he will answer from inside, 'Do not bother me; the door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up and give you anything'?

8I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will get up and give him whatever he needs.

9So I tell you, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

10For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

11Which father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?

12Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?

13If you, then, evil as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!"

The Finger of God

14He was driving out a demon that was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.

15But some of them said, "He drives out the demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons."

16Others, to test Him, were demanding from Him a sign from heaven.

17But He knew their thoughts and said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls on house.

18If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I drive out the demons by Beelzebul.

19If I drive out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So they will be your judges.

20But if it is by the finger of God that I drive out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

21When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are safe;

22but when one stronger than he attacks him and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which he trusted and divides his plunder.

23Whoever is not with Me is against Me, and whoever does not gather with Me scatters.

24"When the unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it passes through waterless places looking for rest; and finding none, it says, 'I will go back to my house that I came out of.'

25When it comes, it finds it swept and put in order.

26Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and live there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first."

27As He was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to Him, "Blessed is the womb that carried You and the breasts that nursed You!"

28But He said, "Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it!"

The Sign of Jonah

29As the crowds were increasing, He began to say, "This generation is an evil generation; it looks for a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah.

30For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.

31The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and something greater than Solomon is here.

32The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and something greater than Jonah is here.

33"No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.

34The lamp of your body is your eye. When your eye is sound, your whole body is full of light; but when it is evil, your body is full of darkness.

35See to it, then, that the light in you is not darkness.

36If your whole body, then, is full of light, with no part of it dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a lamp gives you light with its brightness."

Woes to Pharisees and Lawyers

38The Pharisee was surprised to see that He did not first wash before the meal.

39But the Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of plunder and wickedness.

41But give as alms what is inside, and then everything is clean for you.

42"But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.

43Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seat in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.

46He said, "Woe to you lawyers also! For you load people with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.

47Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and it was your fathers who killed them.

48So you are witnesses, and you approve of the deeds of your fathers; for they killed them, and you build their tombs.

49For this reason also the Wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,'

50so that the blood of all the prophets, shed since the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,

51from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.

52Woe to you lawyers! For you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not go in yourselves, and you hindered those who were going in."

53When He went out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to press Him hard and to question Him closely about many things,

54lying in wait for Him, to catch Him in something He might say.

Ton epiousion, daily, is found in the Bible only in this prayer (here and Matthew 6:11); it may be for the coming day or needed for existence. Hamartias, sins, where Matthew has debts, and then everyone who is indebted to us: Luke keeps the debt in the second line.

  • vv5–13 "at midnight… because of his shamelessness… how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit" — only Luke has the friend at midnight. Anaideia, shamelessness, the friend's boldness in asking. Matthew has give good things (Matthew 7:11); Luke has give the Holy Spirit.

  • vv14–23 "by the finger of God… one stronger than he… divides his plunder" — en daktylō theou, by the finger of God, the words of Pharaoh's magicians, This is the finger of God (Exodus 8:19); Matthew has by the Spirit of God (Matthew 12:28). The stronger one is the one John promised, stronger than I (3:16).

  • vv27–28 "Blessed is the womb that carried You… Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it" — only Luke has this. Menoun, Rather, which both agrees and corrects. Mary herself is called blessed who believed (1:45) and kept His words (2:19, 51).

  • vv29–32 "the sign of Jonah… the queen of the South… the men of Nineveh" — Luke has no three days and three nights (Matthew 12:40): Jonah himself and his preaching are the sign, as the people of Nineveh believed in God (Jonah 3:5). chapters.title: Where Your Treasure Is
chapters.html:
Luke 12

Do Not Be Afraid

1Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered by thousands, so that they were trampling one another, He began to say to His disciples first, "Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

2Nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

3So whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.

4"I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.

5But I will show you whom to fear: fear the One who, after He has killed, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!

6Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.

7Even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

8"I tell you, everyone who acknowledges Me before people, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God;

9but whoever denies Me before people will be denied before the angels of God.

10Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

11When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or what you are to answer, or what you are to say;

12for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you must say."

The Rich Fool

13Someone in the crowd said to Him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."

14He said to him, "Man, who appointed Me a judge or arbiter over you?"

15He said to them, "Watch out, and guard yourselves against all greed; for a person's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions."

16He told them a parable: "The land of a rich man produced plentifully.

17He reasoned to himself, 'What shall I do, for I have nowhere to store my crops?'

18Then he said, 'This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.

19Then I will say to my soul, Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, be merry.'

20But God said to him, 'Fool! This night your soul is required of you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?'

21So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God."

Do Not Worry

22He said to His disciples, "That is why I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.

23For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.

24Consider the ravens: they do not sow or reap, they have no storeroom or barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than the birds!

25Which of you by worrying can add a single cubit to the span of his life?

26If, then, you cannot do even so small a thing, why do you worry about the rest?

27Consider how the lilies grow: they do not labor or spin; yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

28If God so clothes the grass in the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will He clothe you, you of little faith!

29Do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be anxious.

30For all the nations of the world run after these things, and your Father knows that you need them.

31But seek His kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well.

32"Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.

33Sell your possessions and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not wear out, a treasure in heaven that does not fail, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.

34For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

Be Ready

35"Let your belts be fastened and your lamps burning,

36and be like people waiting for their master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once.

37Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds awake when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt, have them recline at table, and come and serve them.

38If he comes in the second watch, or in the third, and finds them so, blessed are they.

39But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.

40You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect."

41Peter said, "Lord, are You telling this parable for us, or for everyone?"

42The Lord said, "Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his master will put in charge of his household servants, to give them their portion of food at the proper time?

43Blessed is that slave whom his master will find doing so when he comes.

44Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

45But if that slave says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming,' and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,

46the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.

47That slave who knew his master's will and did not get ready or act according to his will, will receive a heavy beating.

48But the one who did not know, and did what deserved a beating, will receive a light beating. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much was entrusted, they will ask all the more.

Not Peace but Division

49"I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

50I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

51Do you think that I came to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.

52From now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three.

53They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."

54He also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, at once you say, 'A shower is coming,' and so it happens.

55When you see the south wind blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat,' and it happens.

56Hypocrites! You know how to judge the appearance of the earth and the sky; why do you not know how to judge this present time?

57"Why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

58As you go with your opponent before a magistrate, make an effort on the way to settle with him, or he may drag you before the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

59I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid the very last copper."

Notes

  • vv1–12 "the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy… five sparrows sold for two pennies… the Holy Spirit will teach you" — Luke names the yeast (Mark 8:15). Five sparrows for two pennies, where Matthew has two sparrows sold for a penny (Matthew 10:29); not one of them is forgotten. Gehenna, as Matthew 10:28. Matthew has the Spirit of your Father (Matthew 10:20); Luke has the Holy Spirit.

  • vv13–21 "who appointed Me a judge or arbiter… take your ease, eat, drink, be merry… Fool! This night your soul is required of you" — only Luke has the rich fool. Tis me katestēsen kritēn, who appointed Me a judge, as the Hebrew asked Moses, Who made you a chief and a judge over us? (Exodus 2:14). Eat, drink, be merry is the Preacher's counsel, nothing better under the sun than to eat and drink and be glad (Ecclesiastes 8:15). Psychē, soul, three times: what he spoke to is what is taken. Apaitousin, is required, word for word they demand back, a loan called in.

  • vv22–34 "Consider the ravens… the lilies… little flock… a treasure in heaven" — as Matthew 6:25–33, with ravens where Matthew has the birds of the sky: God gives… the young ravens… when they cry (Psalm 147:9). The raven was unclean (Leviticus 11:15). To mikron poimnion, little flock, only in Luke. Do not be anxious, mē meteōrizesthe, word for word do not be up in the air.

  • vv35–48 "Let your belts be fastened… he will fasten his belt… and serve them… much will be required" — the Passover was eaten with your waists belted (Exodus 12:11). The master who serves his slaves is only in Luke. Oikonomos, steward, where Matthew has slave (Matthew 24:45). Dichotomēsei, will cut him in two, as Matthew 24:51.

  • vv49–53 "I came to cast fire on the earth… a baptism to be baptized with… division" — John said He would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire (3:16). The baptism is His death, as in Mark 10:38. Synechomai, how distressed I am, word for word how I am pressed. The divided house is Micah's, daughter rises against her mother, daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law (Micah 7:6); Matthew has a sword (Matthew 10:34) where Luke has division.

  • vv54–59 "a cloud rising in the west… the south wind… the very last copper" — Lepton, copper, the smallest coin, the widow's coin (Mark 12:42); Matthew has the last penny (Matthew 5:26).

chapters.title: The Narrow Door
chapters.html:
Luke 13

Repent or Perish

1At that very time some were present who told Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

2He answered them, "Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this?

3No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.

4Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they were worse offenders than all the others who live in Jerusalem?

5No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way."

6He told this parable: "A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and found none.

7He said to the vinedresser, 'For three years now I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down; why should it use up the ground?'

8He answered him, 'Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure.

9If it bears fruit next year, well; but if not, you can cut it down.'"

A Woman Set Free on the Sabbath

10He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

11There was a woman who for eighteen years had had a spirit that crippled her; she was bent over and could not stand up straight at all.

12When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said to her, "Woman, you are set free from your weakness."

13He laid His hands on her, and at once she stood up straight and glorified God.

14But the synagogue leader, indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, said to the crowd, "There are six days on which work ought to be done; come on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day."

15The Lord answered him, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?

16This woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound for eighteen long years, ought she not to be set free from this bond on the sabbath day?"

17As He said this, all His opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things being done by Him.

The Mustard Seed and the Yeast

18He said, "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?

19It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and threw into his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches."

20Again He said, "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?

21It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened."

The Narrow Door

22He went through towns and villages, teaching, and making His way to Jerusalem.

23Someone said to Him, "Lord, will only a few be saved?" He said to them,

24"Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.

25Once the master of the house has got up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, open to us,' he will answer you, 'I do not know where you come from.'

26Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.'

27But he will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of wrongdoing!'

28There will be weeping and grinding of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown out.

29People will come from east and west, and from north and south, and recline at table in the kingdom of God.

30Some are last who will be first, and some are first who will be last."

Jerusalem, Jerusalem

31At that very hour some Pharisees came and said to Him, "Get away from here, for Herod wants to kill You."

32He said to them, "Go and tell that fox, 'I am driving out demons and performing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I reach My goal.'

33Yet I must go on My way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

34Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing.

35Your house is left to you. I tell you, you will not see Me until the time comes when you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

Notes

  • vv1–5 "the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices… the tower in Siloam… unless you repent" — two disasters told only in Luke, one by a man's cruelty and one by accident. Opheiletai, offenders, word for word debtors, the word of the prayer (11:4).

  • vv6–9 "a fig tree planted in his vineyard… three years… let it alone this year also" — the fig tree and the vineyard, the prophets' figures for Israel, there are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree (Jeremiah 8:13). Where Mark tells of a fig tree cursed (Mark 11:13–14), Luke tells of one given another year. If it bears fruit next year, well: the Greek leaves the sentence unfinished.

  • vv10–17 "a spirit that crippled her… bent over… six days on which work ought to be done… a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound" — pneuma astheneias, a spirit that crippled her, word for word a spirit of weakness. The leader quotes the commandment, Six days you shall work (Deuteronomy 5:13). Lyei, untie, and lythēnai, be set free, one verb: the ox is untied on the sabbath, so the woman is set free. Idou deka kai oktō etē, eighteen long years, the idou giving the weight of the time.

  • vv18–21 "a mustard seed… became a tree… yeast… three measures of flour" — as Matthew 13:31–33. Three measures is the flour Sarah baked for the three visitors, three measures of fine flour (Genesis 18:6).

  • vv22–30 "making His way to Jerusalem… the narrow door… Depart from me, all you workers of wrongdoing… from east and west" — the journey of 9:51. Matthew has the narrow gate (Matthew 7:13). The master's words are the psalm's, Depart from me, all who do iniquity (Psalm 6:8). The gathering from four directions is the psalm's, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the sea (Psalm 107:3), and the feast is Isaiah's feast of rich food for all peoples (Isaiah 25:6).

  • vv31–33 "Herod wants to kill You… that fox… on the third day I reach My goal… a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem" — teleioumai, I reach My goal, word for word I am completed: His work ends in Jerusalem. Dei, must, as in 9:22.

  • vv34–35 "Jerusalem, Jerusalem… as a hen gathers her brood under her wings… Your house is left to you" — as Matthew 23:37–39, where Matthew has desolate. The wings are God's own, Like an eagle that stirs up its nest… He spread His wings (Deuteronomy 32:11). Your house… left, as Jeremiah warned, this house shall become a desolation (Jeremiah 22:5). The last line is Psalm 118:26, said again at the entry into the city (19:38).

speech.text: Luke 13
Repent or Perish
At that very time some were present who told Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
He answered them, "Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.
Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they were worse offenders than all the others who live in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way."
He told this parable: "A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and found none.
He said to the vinedresser, 'For three years now I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down; why should it use up the ground?'
He answered him, 'Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure.
If it bears fruit next year, well; but if not, you can cut it down.'"
A Woman Set Free on the Sabbath
He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
There was a woman who for eighteen years had had a spirit that crippled her; she was bent over and could not stand up straight at all.
When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said to her, "Woman, you are set free from your weakness."
He laid His hands on her, and at once she stood up straight and glorified God.

But the synagogue leader, indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, said to the crowd, "There are six days on which work ought to be done; come on those days and be healed, and not on the sabbath day."
The Lord answered him, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?
This woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound for eighteen long years, ought she not to be set free from this bond on the sabbath day?"
As He said this, all His opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things being done by Him.
The Mustard Seed and the Yeast
He said, "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and threw into his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches."
Again He said, "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened."
The Narrow Door
He went through towns and villages, teaching, and making His way to Jerusalem.
Someone said to Him, "Lord, will only a few be saved?" He said to them,
"Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
Once the master of the house has got up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, open to us,' he will answer you, 'I do not know where you come from.'
Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.'
But he will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of wrongdoing!'
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown out.
People will come from east and west, and from north and south, and recline at table in the kingdom of God.
Some are last who will be first, and some are first who will be last."
Jerusalem, Jerusalem
At that very hour some Pharisees came and said to Him, "Get away from here, for Herod wants to kill You."
He said to them, "Go and tell that fox, 'I am driving out demons and performing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I reach My goal.'

Your house is left to you. I tell you, you will not see Me until the time comes when you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

chapters.title: The Great Banquet
chapters.html:
Luke 14

At a Pharisee's Table

1One sabbath, when He went to eat bread in the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees, they were watching Him closely.

2There in front of Him was a man who had dropsy.

3Jesus said to the lawyers and Pharisees, "Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath, or not?"

4But they were silent. So He took hold of the man, healed him and sent him away.

5Then He said to them, "Which of you, if your son or your ox falls into a well, will not pull him out at once on the sabbath day?"

6They could not reply to this.

7He told a parable to those who were invited, when He noticed how they chose the places of honor, saying to them,

8"When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited by him,

9and the one who invited you both comes and says to you, 'Give this man your place,' and then in shame you begin to take the lowest place.

10But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will be honored in the presence of all who recline at table with you.

11For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted."

12He also said to the man who had invited Him, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, in case they also invite you in return and you are repaid.

13But when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind;

14and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."

The Great Dinner

15When one of those reclining at table with Him heard this, he said to Him, "Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!"

16But He said to him, "A man was giving a great dinner, and he invited many.

17At the hour for the dinner he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, for everything is now ready.'

18But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it; please have me excused.'

19Another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out; please have me excused.'

20Another said, 'I have married a wife, and so I cannot come.'

21The slave came and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house was angry and said to his slave, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town, and bring in here the poor and the crippled and the blind and the lame.'

22The slave said, 'Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.'

23The master said to the slave, 'Go out to the roads and the hedges and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled.

24For I tell you, none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.'"

The Cost of Following

25Great crowds were going along with Him, and He turned and said to them,

26"If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.

27Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.

28For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to finish it?

29Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it will begin to mock him,

30saying, 'This man began to build and was not able to finish.'

31Or what king, going out to meet another king in war, will not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one who comes against him with twenty thousand?

32If not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.

33So then, none of you who does not renounce all that he has can be My disciple.

34"Salt is good; but if even the salt has lost its taste, how will it be seasoned?

35It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; it is thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."

Notes

  • vv1–6 "to eat bread in the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees… dropsy… your son or your ox falls into a well" — the third sabbath healing in Luke (6:6–11; 13:10–17), again in a Pharisee's house and again with silence. Hydrōpikos, who had dropsy, swollen with fluid. The law told a man to help even his enemy's animal, you shall surely help him with it (Exodus 23:5).

  • vv7–11 "do not recline in the place of honor… Friend, move up higher… the one who humbles himself will be exalted" — the counsel of Proverbs 25:6–7. Prōtoklisia, the place of honor, the first couch at table. The last line is Mary's song, He has brought down rulers from their thrones and lifted up the humble (1:52).

  • vv12–14 "invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind… you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous" — the same four come back in v21. Antapodoma, repaid, three times (vv12, 14): the repayment that counts is God's.

  • vv15–24 "a great dinner… they all alike began to make excuses… I have married a wife… compel people to come in" — the feast of Isaiah, the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food (Isaiah 25:6). Matthew has a king's wedding feast for his son (Matthew 22:2–10). The excuses are the law's own, for a man newly married shall not go out with the army (Deuteronomy 24:5), and for the man who is engaged… Let him go and return to his house (Deuteronomy 20:7), but here the call is to a feast. Anankason, compel, the urging of a host who will not take no.

  • vv25–33 "does not hate his own father and mother… carry his own cross… count the cost… renounce all that he has" — misei, hate, set against Matthew's loves… more than Me (Matthew 10:37): to put second, in the Bible's way of speaking, as Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and Leah was hated (Genesis 29:30–31). Only Luke has the tower and the king. Apotassetai, renounce, the word of saying goodbye (9:61).

  • vv34–35 "if even the salt has lost its taste… neither for the soil nor for the manure pile" — mōranthē, has lost its taste, word for word has become foolish, as Matthew 5:13.
